subject: ClearPay service impact — transparency readout & next-step timeline
messages:
From: Alex Morton <amorton@clearpay.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>; Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@clearpay.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 22:05:12 -0800
Subject: 12/14 service impact — request for RCA

Ben / Irene,

Thanks for the update over the weekend. We experienced a ~45 minute degradation in API responsiveness for a subset of production ingestion jobs during our peak window (approx 19:40–20:25 UTC). That caused several downstream batch jobs to fail and an outage in our reconciliation pipeline.

Can you share a brief RCA timeline and the immediate mitigation steps you took? Our security and legal teams are asking for a short write-up (high level is fine) so we can file this with internal stakeholders. If you have any logs or a short PDF we can circulate, that would help.

We'd also like to schedule a 30-minute readout tomorrow morning PST to walk through the timeline and next steps.

Thanks —
Alex
Alex Morton
Head of SRE, ClearPay
amorton@clearpay.com
+1 415-555-0199

---

Note: attaching a copy of our incident checklist would be useful once you have it.
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morton <amorton@clearpay.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>; David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>; Priya Singh <priya.singh@clearpay.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Dec 2026 06:10:03 -0800
Subject: Re: 12/14 service impact — request for RCA

Alex —

Really sorry for the disruption. We started an immediate investigation after we saw the errors in our observability platform and prioritized ClearPay traffic for mitigation. High-level summary now and will follow with a structured RCA and timeline (PDF + raw log extract) by 08:30 PST:

- What happened (short): A partial KV cache eviction stressed the routing layer when a high fan-in tenant-specific prefix caused many cold requests to fall back to a slower codepath. This produced a burst of longer-tail token latencies and contributed to request timeouts for a subset of your ingestion endpoints.
- Immediate mitigation: We applied a temporary routing rule to pin ClearPay traffic to a cold-start-optimized pool and increased autoscaling headroom for the affected pool.
- Next steps (we will deliver): full timeline, owner assignments, and compensatory controls (config and code fixes).

Irene is leading the tech write-up; David is pulling the logs. We'll attach the PDF RCA and the eviction log.

Can we do 08:45–09:15 PST tomorrow for the readout?

Ben Carter
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morton <amorton@clearpay.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>; David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>; Priya Singh <priya.singh@clearpay.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Dec 2026 08:25:17 -0800
Subject: ClearPay service impact — transparency readout & next-step timeline

Alex / Priya —

Attached: clearpay_rca.pdf (concise RCA), kv-eviction-log-20261214.txt (eviction events around 19:20–20:40 UTC). Below is the customer-facing summary and the action timeline we will own. If anything is missing or you want different formatting for your audit, tell us and we will adapt.

RCA summary (executive):
- Incident window: 2026-12-14 19:20:00 UTC — 2026-12-14 20:05:00 UTC (impact apparent 19:40–20:25 UTC).
- Impact: Intermittent request timeouts and elevated token generation latency for a subset of ClearPay ingestion endpoints; downstream reconciliation jobs retried and failed for several batches. No customer PII exposure identified in our review.
- Root cause: Tenant-specific KV cache eviction cascade + routing fallback to non-quantized inference paths for affected requests. The combination caused a burst of long-tail latencies and transient overloads on a small set of serving workers.

Timeline (abbreviated):
- 19:18 UTC: Increase in cache pressure observed; preliminary alerts flagged KV eviction spikes.
- 19:25 UTC: Error rates for ClearPay ingestion begin to rise; some requests moved to fallback codepath.
- 19:40 UTC: Customer-facing impact becomes measurable; ClearPay batch jobs start failing.
- 19:42 UTC: Automated mitigation (scale-up) triggered but insufficient due to headroom config.
- 19:50 UTC: Manual routing rule applied to pin ClearPay traffic to optimized pool (temporary fix).
- 20:00 UTC: Autoscale headroom increased; error rates decline.
- 20:05–20:25 UTC: Final verification and phased rollback of temporary routing rules; monitoring confirms recovery.

Action items & owners (target dates):
- Short-term (0–48h):
  - Deploy a targeted configuration change to increase default pool headroom for high-fan-in tenants (owner: David Kim) — ETA: 2026-12-16
  - Add an automated detection rule for bursty eviction patterns (owner: Irene Choi) — ETA: 2026-12-17
- Medium-term (2–6 weeks):
  - Implement a tenant-aware routing optimization that prevents cold-request fan-in for large ingestion jobs (owner: Serving Runtime team / David Kim) — ETA: 2027-01-20
  - Quantization-safe fallback: ensure fallback codepath uses a quantized runtime where possible to avoid slow non-quantized paths (owner: Runtime Optimizations) — ETA: 2027-01-12
- Long-term (quarter):
  - Improve multi-tenant eviction resilience with backpressure controls and better KV hot-key detection (owner: Platform Resilience) — ETA: 2027-03-31

Compensation / credits: We will follow our SLA process and propose a customer credit to ClearPay once you confirm the impacted envelope of requests. If you prefer, we can pre-seed a provisional credit while we finalize scope.

Attachments: clearpay_rca.pdf (4-page summary & timeline), kv-eviction-log-20261214.txt (truncated, first 10k lines).

If you want a technical deep-dive, Irene can cover data from the logs and David can walk the exact trace examples in the call. Proposed readout: Wed 08:45–09:15 PST.

Thanks again for your patience — we take this seriously and will run through corrective actions and verification with you.

—
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
